findings.evidence: scripts/HeaderStyle.lean:51 `discard <| lintModules opts #[] (args.toArray.map pathToModule) .exceptionsFile false`; TextBased.lean:520-535 lints each supplied module's file; TextBased.lean:264 `formatErrors` prints to stdout; scripts/lint-style.sh:73-78 already computes the other comm direction from the same keys.
findings.fix: Keep one pass: add `comm -13 "$lint_src/baseline.keys" "$lint_src/actual.keys"` as the new-violation gate, pass `TauCeti.lean` alongside the discovered files so the empty root is linted too, and delete the `lake exe lint-style` invocation together with the generated `TauCetiLint/All.lean`, the `LEAN_SRC_PATH` plumbing and the import-count assertion it exists to protect. If the module-name check matters, call the public `modulesOSForbidden` (TextBased.lean:601) from HeaderStyle.lean instead of re-running the full lint.
findings.issue: The whole text lint runs twice: `HeaderStyle.lean` already calls `lintModules opts #[] <all files> .exceptionsFile` (scripts/HeaderStyle.lean:51), which lints exactly those files and prints every violation to stdout (captured as actual.keys); `lake exe lint-style TauCetiLint.All TauCeti` then re-lints the same files to report the unbaselined subset. That subset is `comm -13 baseline.keys actual.keys` — Mathlib's exception matching is exactly the wrapper's key (Mathlib/Tactic/Linter/TextBased.lean:163-176 `compare` ignores the line number and compares path + StyleError; :191 prints `path : line N : CODE : message`), so the second pass derives nothing the first pass did not already produce.

findings.evidence: scripts/ModuleSystem.lean:30-31 and scripts/Axioms.lean:45-46 both define `def pathToModule (p : System.FilePath) : Name := (p.withExtension "").components.foldl (fun n s => Name.mkStr n s) Name.anonymous`.
findings.fix: Reuse the existing definition — factor `pathToModule` (and, if the enumeration stays, `collectLeanModules`) into one shared module imported by `scripts.Axioms`, `scripts.ModuleSystem` and this audit (making the audit a `lean_exe` root like the other two), rather than adding a third variant.
findings.issue: `pathToModule` is a third copy of a helper that already exists twice in this repo, in a weaker form: `(path.dropEnd 5).toString.splitOn "/"` instead of the existing `(p.withExtension "").components` (which is separator- and `./`-robust, hence the shell-side path regex needed to prop it up).

findings.evidence: scripts/lint-env.sh:238 `find TauCeti -name '*.lean' | LC_ALL=C sort | sed 's/\.lean$//; s|/|.|g' > "$MODULE_IMPORT_LIST"` and :247 `sed 's/^/import /' "$MODULE_IMPORT_LIST"`; scripts/ModuleSystem.lean:33-47 `collectLeanModules`/`auditedModules`.
findings.fix: Factor one discovery routine (a sourced shell helper emitting the NUL-safe, validated file/module list) and have lint-env.sh's driver generation consume it, so the audited set and its validation have a single definition.
findings.issue: Source discovery and import-root generation are a near-clone of scripts/lint-env.sh, which already enumerates `TauCeti/**/*.lean` and emits an import-all driver for the same reason (empty root); `scripts/ModuleSystem.lean` does the same enumeration in Lean. Three independent enumerations of the audited tree can drift, and only this one validates paths/symlinks.

summary: The wrapper runs Mathlib's full text-based lint twice over the same ~2,500 sources, and re-implements module-path and source-discovery helpers that already exist in scripts/ModuleSystem.lean, scripts/Axioms.lean and scripts/lint-env.sh.
